attributes.title: Detección automática de ambigüedad en requisitos funcionales: un estudio de caso en el dominio de trazabilidad cárnica (CarniCore)
attributes.description: Este preregistro documenta el protocolo experimental del componente empírico del proyecto CarniCore. El estudio evalúa la precisión de un detector automático de ambigüedad y malos olores en requisitos funcionales, comparando su clasificación con el consenso de personas expertas mediante métricas de exactitud y coeficientes de concordancia.

344-2.value:
RQ1: How accurately can an automatic ambiguity detector replicate the judgment of expert evaluators when identifying ambiguous functional requirements in the CarniCore requirements specification?
H0: The agreement between the automatic ambiguity detector and the expert consensus is not greater than would be expected by chance (Cohen's κ ≤ 0). Equivalently, the detector's F1-score does not differ from that of a random classifier with the same prevalence of ambiguous requirements.
H1: The agreement between the automatic ambiguity detector and the expert consensus is significantly greater than would be expected by chance (Cohen's κ > 0).

344-40.value:
This study is an observational diagnostic accuracy study with a cross-sectional and census-based design. The complete population of 25 functional requirements (RF-01 to RF-25) from the CarniCore Software Requirements Specification is analyzed; therefore, no sampling is performed.

Each functional requirement is independently classified by two sources: (1) an automatic ambiguity detector based on predefined textual patterns, and (2) a panel of at least three expert evaluators who classify each requirement as "ambiguous" or "not ambiguous". The expert evaluators perform their assessments independently and are blinded to both the detector's output and the classifications made by the other evaluators.

The unit of analysis is the individual functional requirement. Because every requirement is evaluated by both classification methods, the design uses paired observations. To reduce ordering effects, the functional requirements are presented to each expert in a randomized order generated with a fixed random seed. The primary outcomes are precision, recall, F1-score, Cohen's kappa, and Fleiss' kappa, which quantify the agreement between the automatic detector and the expert consensus.

344-47.value:
The study uses a census-based sampling strategy and therefore includes the complete population of 25 functional requirements (RF-01 to RF-25) defined in the CarniCore Software Requirements Specification. No probabilistic sampling is performed.

The study also recruits a minimum of three expert evaluators (five recommended) with academic or professional experience in Requirements Engineering or Software Engineering. Eligible participants must not be members of the CarniCore development team and must be able to independently classify all 25 functional requirements. Expert evaluators are recruited voluntarily and provide informed consent before participation.

Data collection consists of two stages. First, the automatic ambiguity detector analyzes the complete set of functional requirements and produces an initial binary classification (ambiguous or not ambiguous). Second, each expert independently classifies the same requirements without access to the detector's results or the assessments of other experts. The order of presentation of the requirements is randomized for each evaluator using a fixed random seed to reduce ordering effects.

Data collection will take place during the experimental phase of the CarniCore project after protocol registration and before statistical analysis. All collected data, expert classifications, detector outputs, and derived metrics will be stored in the project's version-controlled experimental repository.

344-51.value:
The unit of analysis is the individual functional requirement. The study includes the complete census of 25 functional requirements (RF-01 to RF-25) defined in the CarniCore Software Requirements Specification; therefore, no sampling is performed at the requirement level.

Each functional requirement will be independently evaluated by two sources: (1) the automatic ambiguity detector and (2) a panel of expert evaluators. The expert panel will include a minimum of three evaluators (five recommended). Consequently, each of the 25 functional requirements will receive one automated classification and at least three independent expert classifications.

No statistical power analysis was performed because the study analyzes the complete population of functional requirements rather than a probabilistic sample.

344-55.value:
No pilot study will be conducted. Data collection will begin only after (1) this preregistration has been completed, (2) the set of 25 functional requirements has been finalized and frozen, and (3) the expert evaluators have been recruited and have provided informed consent.

Data collection will end when all 25 functional requirements have been independently classified by the automatic ambiguity detector and by at least three expert evaluators. No additional requirements or expert evaluations will be added after data collection has been completed. Statistical analysis will begin only after the complete dataset has been collected and verified.

344-62.value:
The primary measured variable is the binary classification assigned to each functional requirement (Ambiguous / Not Ambiguous). This classification is obtained independently from two sources: (1) the automatic ambiguity detector and (2) the expert evaluators.

The primary outcome measures are the detector's precision, recall, and F1-score, calculated against the expert consensus. Inter-rater agreement will be assessed using Cohen's kappa for expert pairs and Fleiss' kappa for the complete panel of experts.

Additional recorded variables include the source of each classification (detector or expert), the functional requirement identifier (RF-01 to RF-25), the ambiguity category identified by experts (vague quantifier, multiple conjunctions, passive voice without explicit agent, or other), and the confidence level reported by each expert using a five-point Likert scale.

Control variables include the fixed set of 25 functional requirements, the common operational definition of ambiguity, blinded expert evaluation, and a randomized presentation order of requirements.

344-66.value:
Derived variables will be calculated from the binary classifications (Ambiguous / Not Ambiguous) assigned by the automatic ambiguity detector and the expert consensus.

The expert consensus will be established by majority vote among the expert evaluators. This consensus will be used as the reference standard (ground truth).

The following performance metrics will be computed from the confusion matrix:

- Precision = TP / (TP + FP)
- Recall = TP / (TP + FN)
- F1-score = 2 × (Precision × Recall) / (Precision + Recall)

Inter-rater agreement will be measured using Cohen's kappa for pairwise agreement between experts and Fleiss' kappa for agreement among the complete panel of experts.

No additional composite indices or transformations will be applied.

344-71.value:
The primary analysis compares the binary classifications produced by the automatic ambiguity detector with the expert consensus.

The expert consensus, determined by majority vote among the expert evaluators, will be used as the reference standard (ground truth).

The following statistical analyses will be performed:

1. Descriptive statistics summarizing the number and proportion of functional requirements classified as ambiguous and not ambiguous by the detector and by each expert evaluator.

2. Construction of a confusion matrix comparing the detector classifications with the expert consensus.

3. Calculation of diagnostic performance measures:
   - Precision
   - Recall (Sensitivity)
   - F1-score

4. Assessment of inter-rater agreement:
   - Cohen's kappa for each pair of expert evaluators.
   - Fleiss' kappa for agreement among the complete expert panel.

5. Hypothesis testing:
   The null hypothesis (H0: κ ≤ 0) will be evaluated using the asymptotic standard error of Cohen's kappa with a significance level of α = 0.05. If multiple pairwise kappa significance tests are performed, Bonferroni correction will be applied.

The analyses will be implemented in Python using scikit-learn for diagnostic performance metrics and statsmodels.stats.inter_rater for Cohen's kappa and Fleiss' kappa. No regression models, ANOVA, structural equation models, or causal models will be used because the study is observational and compares classification agreement rather than causal effects.

344-75.value:
The primary outcome variable is binary and will be coded as follows:

- Ambiguous = 1
- Not Ambiguous = 0

The source of each classification will be recorded as:
- Automatic detector
- Expert evaluator

Expert consensus will be obtained by majority vote among the expert evaluators and will be used as the reference standard for all performance analyses.

No centering, scaling, normalization, or mathematical transformations will be applied to the data before analysis. The confusion matrix, precision, recall, F1-score, Cohen's kappa, and Fleiss' kappa will be calculated directly from the original binary classifications.

344-77.value:
Statistical inference will be based on a significance level of α = 0.05.

The primary hypothesis will be evaluated using Cohen's kappa to assess agreement between the automatic ambiguity detector and the expert consensus. The null hypothesis states that agreement is not greater than chance (κ ≤ 0), whereas the alternative hypothesis states that agreement is greater than chance (κ > 0).

The significance of Cohen's kappa will be evaluated using its asymptotic standard error. Because the alternative hypothesis specifies greater agreement than chance, a one-tailed test will be used.

If multiple pairwise Cohen's kappa significance tests are performed, Bonferroni correction will be applied to control the family-wise error rate.

In addition to statistical significance, the practical interpretation of the results will emphasize effect sizes, including Cohen's kappa, precision, recall, and F1-score. Statistical analyses will be conducted using Python with scikit-learn and statsmodels.

344-79.value:
All 25 functional requirements (RF-01 to RF-25) included in the final frozen version of the CarniCore Software Requirements Specification will be analyzed. No functional requirement will be excluded unless it is withdrawn from the specification before the start of data collection.

Expert evaluations will be included only if the evaluator completes the classification of all 25 functional requirements and meets the predefined eligibility criteria (experience in Requirements Engineering or Software Engineering, not being a member of the CarniCore development team, and providing informed consent).

Incomplete expert evaluations will be excluded from the analysis. No statistical outlier detection or removal procedures will be applied because the study uses binary categorical classifications rather than continuous measurements.

344-81.value:
Missing data are not expected because each expert evaluator will be required to complete the classification of all 25 functional requirements before the evaluation is considered valid.

If an expert does not complete the full assessment, that evaluator's responses will be excluded from the statistical analyses and replaced, if necessary, to maintain the minimum required number of expert evaluators. No imputation methods will be used for missing data.

The final analyses will be performed only on complete datasets containing classifications for all 25 functional requirements.
